blocking.problem:
A matched non-permutation computation/adjoint on clean workspace is never recognized as restoring its known-zero entry before a subsequent borrow frame. Memoryless ptr_width=32 signature: {"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}. Exact function (LF after every line):
action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()
^entry():
c = qalloc any 1
h c
h c
b = qborrow any 1
cx c b
qreturn b
qfree c
Store interface/closure H=12efae749cb84eec0918c9aa49adb348957eba9e81e0eaa8f2514481a0d9dba0 in the usual sole symbol 0; with the canonical 0.8 header, section symbols, blank line and section functions, object_hash=b2534762bf5eb795efd7ba74195198f0b67e2012b9f3243700e58ee92ee9fc53. Independently built those bytes and hashes with Python, without Object::parse. check and run-action /dev/stdin a --mut 0 both exit 1, empty stdout, '§5.6: a wire released inside a borrow frame is not clean'. Hand: H^2=I, so c=0 before CX; CX(0,b)=I for every unknown b and any entangled reference, and c is freed clean. The entire action is identity on t and bR. factorises replays each Other(H c) by replacing c with a new unrelated Boolean variable, so the second H cannot restore c=0. This is a definite rejection, not an unresolved opaque claim. No token or execution budget is involved.

With the new round-6 prefix replay, that truncated circuit supplies incorrect reachable entry facts, and an invalid borrowed operation is admitted. ^entry():
c = qalloc any 1
x c
qloop 4 {
h t
x c
}
b = qborrow any 1
cx c b
qreturn b
h t
x c
qfree c
Interface/closure H=232f157c4fe6c4abdb3ebc384d1b19b01751b68df4949b86d25996e87c300515; stored-H object_hash=3e8f134a472e3e31545e6bd3ec22058da463927ea24af3929bf3357a36ca3926 (canonical sole-symbol object, independently hashed). check /dev/stdin exits 0/status ok. run-action /dev/stdin a --mut 0 then exits 1, empty stdout, '§5.6: borrowed wires were not returned to their entry state'. summary:
Reviewed the complete 39,749-line prompt in slices no larger than 1,500 lines, including the round-6 diff first, the settled specification and all 92 embedded crate files. All four previous IDs are resolved on their exact witnesses: SOL-R6-B01/R6-B02 (disjoint-boundary clean facts) and SOL-R6-B02/R6-B01 (executed lifetime widths). Two new core S0 defects and one contract S0 defect require revision.
Mandatory methods completed, using spec derivations before treating executable/test output as corroboration: (1) Hand-derived inc8's LF-terminated nine-line identity envelope and tight-budget results, plus sum_db(2)'s 38 rows, payload 3, 48-cell stack requirement and stack-47 fault at row 29. Independent hashlib and the CLI agree with the inc8 digest and the tuples (3,0,38), (0,1,37), (0,3,29); inc8 at B=3/2/0 gives (0,0,3)/(0,1,2)/(0,1,0). Also traced ret's restored-fp delivery and the §7.4 nested @f/@g clock segment: inner reversed frames and markers are skipped by outer reversal, clock/tape return to zero, pure copied result survives; runtime reverse confirms complete entry restoration. (3) Audited every SPEC-QUESTIONS entry 1–30 against the relevant specification sentences; the documented choices are defensible, including explicit staged Unverified routes. The new issues are implementation errors, not requests to change the settled spec. (4) Ran the exact required search patterns over the crate and classified the hits: test assertions/helpers and cfg(test) unwraps; fallible json Parser::expect; internal ASCII/positive-width/header/hex/label/queue/Tarjan/running-control invariants; explicit unsupported registry/model/cleanup diagnostics; and numerical display approximation. No todo!/unimplemented! stub was found. The display-conversion hits led to SOL-R7-B03; they were not accepted merely because they were labelled diagnostic. The Python seed is an untrusted limited aid. (5) Cross-checked the complete row/opcode lists, all 11 fault codes, history/frame kinds, schema fields and CLI dispatches against object.rs/schema.rs/validation.rs, oracle.rs/machine.rs, classical.rs/action.rs/quantum.rs, identity/metadata/certificate and main.rs.
